text: A 34-year-old accountant has worried most days for about 8 months about money, her children's health and small mistakes at work. She says she cannot switch the worry off. text: A 41-year-old man has worried most days for over a year about work and family. He finds it hard to stop, but apart from feeling tired easily and some irritability he reports no other physical or mental signs.
label: misses
evidence_query: subthreshold generalized anxiety symptoms fewer associated symptoms
why: Does not fit Generalized anxiety disorder: criterion C fails (In adults, at least 3 of 6 physical or mental signs go with the worry, some present more days than not.) Here only 2 of the needed signs are described: tiring easily, irritability.

text: A 36-year-old woman worries most days for 7 months, but nearly all of the worry is about being attacked again after an assault: she avoids the street where it happened, wakes from nightmares about it and startles at loud noises. She is tense, irritable and sleeps poorly.
label: misses
evidence_query: differentiating PTSD from generalized anxiety disorder worry trauma reminders
why: Does not fit Generalized anxiety disorder: criterion F fails (Not better explained by another mental disorder, such as fear of a trauma reminder in PTSD or obsessions in OCD.) Here the picture is better explained by Posttraumatic stress disorder (adults).

text: A 24-year-old student has felt anxious, restless and unable to sleep for 7 months, all of it starting when he began taking high doses of stimulants bought online to study; he worries about many things and cannot stop.
label: misses
evidence_query: substance-induced anxiety disorder stimulant use
why: Does not fit Generalized anxiety disorder: criterion E fails (Not caused by a substance or a medical condition.) Here the symptoms are tied to stimulant use.

text: Since losing his job and going through a divorce 6 months ago, a 45-year-old man has replayed the events, avoids old colleagues, feels hopeless, sleeps badly and is irritable.
label: misses
evidence_query: criterion A traumatic event non-traumatic stressors adjustment disorder

text: Four months after an assault, a 30-year-old woman has nightmares about it, avoids the bar where it happened, feels persistent shame and fear, and has trouble sleeping, but is not on guard, irritable, reckless or jumpy.

why: Does not fit Posttraumatic stress disorder (adults): criterion E fails (At least 2 changes in arousal or reactivity that began or worsened after the event: irritability or anger, reckless behavior, hypervigilance, strong startle, poor concentration, sleep problems.)
